stage_2_story.text_en:
Last Friday morning, Moshe drove his two grandchildren, Noa and Yonatan, to their swimming competition at the Ramat Gan municipal pool. Moshe had never been to a swim meet before, and Noa promised to explain everything.

When they arrived, the pool was busy. Eight lanes stretched from one end to the other, and swimmers were warming up, counting their laps back and forth. Noa adjusted her goggles and tied her cap tightly. Yonatan looked nervous.

'Your first race is freestyle,' Moshe read from the programme. 'What does that mean?' Noa smiled. 'It means you can swim any style you like, Saba — but everyone swims freestyle because it is the fastest.'

Yonatan was first up. He stood on the starting block, bent his knees, and made a clean dive into the water. The crowd clapped. He swam with a powerful stroke all the way to the other end and came back without stopping. He finished second in his lane.

Noa competed in the backstroke event. She lay back in the water and pushed off the wall smoothly. Moshe watched her face pointing up at the ceiling lights as she glided along. She won her heat.

The final event of the morning was a relay. Noa swam butterfly for her team's first leg — the hardest stroke of all. She handed off to her teammate with a clean touch. Their team finished third overall.

On the drive home, Moshe bought the children falafel and sat quietly for a moment. 'Next time,' he said, 'I want to swim one lap myself.' Noa laughed and said, 'We will teach you, Saba. First lesson: goggles on.'
